title: The benefit-of-the-doubt restaurant rule
allegory: UCB is choosing tonight's restaurant in a new town by its average rating so far plus a benefit of the doubt that shrinks every time you eat there and slowly grows back for places you keep skipping.

chapters.name: Try or stick?
chapters.note: a month of dinners, ten restaurants

cap.1: New town, ten restaurants, a month of dinners. Keep going to the good one you found, or try others that might be better? Every test night has a cost.
cap.2: A multi-armed bandit: arms with unknown average payouts and limited pulls. Exploring costs reward now; exploiting risks never finding a better arm.
cap.3: The k-armed bandit is a one-state MDP: exploration versus exploitation with no credit assignment, scored by regret against always pulling the best arm.

cap.1: The rule: every place gets a benefit of the doubt that shrinks each time you eat there. Each night, go wherever average plus doubt is highest.
cap.2: UCB scores each arm as its mean so far plus an uncertainty bonus. Rarely tried arms get a big bonus, so they get tried; well-known arms are judged on their mean.
cap.3: Optimism under uncertainty: act greedily on an upper confidence bound, not the point estimate. Unlike ε-greedy, exploration is aimed at the uncertain arms.

cap.1: The doubt grows slowly with the total nights so far and shrinks with visits to this place. Skip a place long enough and its doubt creeps back up.
cap.2: Bonus = c·√(ln t / N_a): four times as many visits halve it, and ln t slowly regrows it for arms you neglect. c sets how bold the exploring is.
cap.3: UCB1, Sutton and Barto eq. 2.10. Auer, Cesa-Bianchi and Fischer (2002) proved logarithmic regret bounds uniformly over time, which makes it more than a heuristic.

cap.1: The more you eat somewhere, the less benefit of the doubt it gets: four visits halve it. As the month goes on, doubt creeps back for places you skipped.
cap.2: The bonus falls like 1/√N_a with visits and rises like √(ln t) with time, so neglected arms always get revisited eventually.
cap.3: Bonus ∝ √(ln t / N_a): ln t is unbounded, so no arm is abandoned forever, yet it grows slowly enough that pulls of bad arms grow only logarithmically.

chapters.name: Night one breaks
chapters.verdict: Guard the divide with something tiny, and reset N and Q in reset().

cap.1: On night one you have eaten nowhere, and 'divide by zero visits' breaks the rule. Give untried places near-endless doubt so each gets one visit first.
cap.2: N_a = 0 makes the bonus infinite or NaN. Add a tiny epsilon (ARENA's skeleton passes 1e-6) so untried arms go first; a big one quietly turns UCB into greedy.
cap.3: A large epsilon collapses the bonus and degenerates UCB to greedy on Q. Also initialise N and Q inside reset, after super().reset(seed), with Q stored as float.

chapters.name: Where it goes
items: A bonus section: nothing later depends on it
Inside tree search: PUCT adds a learned prior
With delayed feedback, Thompson sampling won

cap.1: This one is a bonus: nothing later in the course needs it. But the same benefit-of-the-doubt idea steers the tree search behind AlphaZero.
cap.2: PUCT, the selection rule inside MCTS, is UCB plus a learned prior over moves. What an agent explores decides what it can ever learn, and so what behaviour you end up with.
cap.3: Chapelle and Li (2011), Yahoo traffic with an hour of click delay: Thompson sampling 59,256 regret vs UCB 226,220. A deterministic index re-picks one arm while evidence is in flight.

caption.1: Slide boldness to zero and you always pick A, the best average. Raise it and barely tried D wins the night. Give B more visits and watch its doubt shrink.
caption.2: Each bar is average plus benefit of the doubt. Low c is nearly greedy; high c explores whatever you know least. More nights (t) slowly inflate every bonus.
caption.3: argmax_a Q_a + c√(ln t / N_a): c trades exploration against exploitation, N_a shrinks a bonus as 1/√N_a, and ln t regrows it for neglected arms.

hamming.what: A rule that picks the option with the best average so far plus a benefit-of-the-doubt bonus that shrinks with every try.
hamming.when: When you must keep choosing among options with unknown payoffs and pay for every test: bandits, and the selection step inside tree search.
hamming.why: It aims exploration at what you know least instead of at random, which provably keeps the total cost of exploring low.

object.title: The doubt landscape
object.subtitle: Height is the benefit of the doubt: a cliff where you have barely tried, a gentle rise as nights pass.

marks.label: barely tried, late in the month

cap.1: Height is the benefit of the doubt: tall where you have barely tried a place, low where you know it well.
cap.2: Height = c·√(ln t / N): one axis is nights so far, the other is visits to this arm.
cap.3: The UCB1 exploration bonus as a function of total pulls t and this arm's pulls N_a.

cap.1: Along the visits direction the cliff drops fast: every visit trims the doubt, and four visits halve it.
cap.2: The bonus falls as 1/√N: most of the doubt is burned off by the first few tries.
cap.3: ∂bonus/∂N ∝ −N^(−3/2): early pulls buy most of the information.

cap.1: Along the nights direction the rise is gentle: places you skip slowly regain some doubt, so none is given up forever.
cap.2: √(ln t) grows without limit but very slowly, which guarantees revisits without wasting many pulls.
cap.3: Unbounded but sublinear growth in t is what yields logarithmic regret: bad arms are revisited, but rarely.

cap.1: Set boldness to zero and the landscape goes flat: no doubt anywhere, just picking the best average. That is pure greed.
cap.2: c = 0 reduces UCB to greedy selection on the mean, which can lock onto an arm after one lucky pull.
cap.3: c scales the confidence width; c = 0 removes optimism entirely and with it the exploration guarantee.

cap.1: Turn boldness up and the whole landscape rises: more exploring, less cashing in.
cap.2: Large c explores more; the right value depends on how noisy the payouts are.
cap.3: c trades regret from under-exploration against regret from over-exploration; it is tuned to the reward scale and noise.

predict.q: Two places have the same average. You have visited one 20 times and the other twice. Which does UCB pick?

options.t: The one visited twice: it has more benefit of the doubt
The one visited 20 times: it is better known

predict.why: Same average, so the bigger bonus wins, and fewer visits means a bigger bonus.

predict.q: Your UCB agent locks onto one arm after an unlucky start. Likely bug?

options.t: A big epsilon in the visits denominator squashed the bonus
Boldness c is set too high

predict.why: With the bonus squashed, UCB is just greedy on the average and never revisits an arm that started unlucky.

predict.q: How does UCB's exploring differ from ε-greedy's?

options.t: UCB explores where it is least certain; ε-greedy explores at random

predict.why: ε-greedy picks random arms uniformly; UCB aims its exploration at the arms it knows least about.

object.where: Anywhere tries cost something: bandits, tree search, adaptive experiments.
